cards.text: Stephen, a follower of Jesus, is on trial before the Sanhedrin, the Jewish ruling council (Acts 6:12-15). When the high priest asks if the charges are true, Stephen answers with Israel's history from Abraham all the way to Moses and the calf (Acts 7:1-43), and friend, he is NOT done yet. Now he gets to the tent their fathers had with them in the wilderness: the tabernacle of the Testimony.

cards.question: The tabernacle in the wilderness was built however the workers thought looked best.

cards.text: That tent goes the distance, friend. The fathers bring it into the land with Joshua, Israel's leader after Moses, when God drives the nations out before them.

cards.question: How long does the tabernacle last in the land? It remains until the time of ___.

cards.text: That's David, king of Israel, and he found favor in the sight of God. He asks to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.

cards.question: David is the one who asks. But the one who actually builds the house for God is his son ___.

cards.text: Solomon, David's son, builds the house. Then Stephen turns a corner, and now he's talking about where the Most High lives.

cards.question: Stephen tells the council that the Most High dwells in houses made by human hands.

cards.text: Stephen backs it up with the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 66:1-2). The Lord says, "Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool."

cards.question: In the words Stephen quotes, the Lord says heaven is His throne and the earth is His footstool. Then what does the Lord ask about?

answers.text: What house could be built for Him
What gift could be brought to Him
What song could be sung to Him

cards.text: Then Stephen turns from the history to the council itself. No warm-up, no "with all due respect," just: "You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears!"

cards.question: Stephen tells the council they always resist someone, just as their fathers did. Who?

cards.text: Then he asks them, "Which of the prophets did your fathers fail to persecute?" That's the kind of question where everybody in the room suddenly gets REAL interested in their own sandals.

cards.question: Stephen says the council's fathers even killed the prophets who foretold the coming of the Righteous One.
Now Stephen points it at the council members themselves. What does he call them when it comes to the Righteous One?
Stephen ends his speech: the council received the law ordained by angels, yet they have not ___ it.

cards.text: On hearing this, the members of the Sanhedrin are enraged, and they gnash their teeth at Stephen. That room has OFFICIALLY stopped taking questions.

cards.question: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looks intently into heaven and sees the glory of God. Who does he see standing at the right hand of God?

cards.text: And Stephen says it right out loud: "I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God." Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

cards.question: When Stephen says he sees heaven open, the council calms down and listens closely.

cards.text: They cover their ears, cry out in a loud voice and rush at him together. They drag him out of the city and begin to stone him.
Meanwhile, the witnesses lay their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul. And while they're stoning him, Stephen calls out to the Lord.

cards.question: As the stones come, Stephen asks the Lord Jesus to receive his ___.

cards.text: Then Stephen falls on his knees and cries out in a loud voice.

cards.question: On his knees, with the stones still coming, Stephen asks the Lord to hold this sin against them.

cards.text: He asks the Lord NOT to hold this sin against the very people stoning him, and when he has said this, he falls asleep. Friend, I need a minute with that one.

cards.question: Saul, the young man who had the witnesses' garments at his feet, gives approval to Stephen's death.

cards.text: On that day, a great persecution breaks out against the church in Jerusalem. Everyone in the church except the apostles is scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.

cards.question: After Stephen's death, who buries him and mourns deeply over him?
Saul begins to destroy the church. Going from house to house, what does he do?

answers.text: Drags men and women off to prison
Burns their houses to the ground
